col4_Comment:
School Food programmes in Cape Town as well as nutrition programmes for children and pregnant mothers are led by the Provincial Government and are managed by multiple departments. There is no single database for food consumption data but this is an identified area of work under the City of Cape Town's transversal Food Systems Working Group of City Officials and external partners, such as universities and NGOs, who have greatly contributed towards the City's growing understanding of the system, its complexity and the City's potential role. 

The City launched a Food Systems programme in July 2021, which has since been included in the City's overall master plan, the Integrated Development Plan (2022-2027). There is limited city-scale data on food production, consumption or food security available for Cape Town and institutionally the governance of this area is still in development in the municipality as it has predominantly been a national and provincial mandate. Since the Food Systems Programme was launched in 2021 a programme review process was conducted to evaluate progress and the way forward. The Food Systems Programme Implementation Review Report was completed in 2025 under this Programme, and several studies have been conducted assessing the resilience and structure of food systems at a city-wide and provincial level but neither provide the updated and complete figures required for this section. 

Food provision programmes include: 
•	The City's Safe Spaces programme (July 2024-June 2025) is ongoing and has a budget of R9 900 000 allocated for the development and extension of safe spaces. The Safe Space Programme offers bed accommodation and additional supportive services for individuals experiencing homelessness, with the overarching goal of fostering opportunities that support their successful reintegration into society. Part of the services received are meals. Over the financial year the four Safe Space sites have provided 604 060 meals (July 2024-June 2025). 
•	The City's Winter Readiness Programme provides dry ingredients (food), blankets and matrasses to expand bed spaces at shelters during winter and the City's Disaster Risk Management Centre disburses (donated) food aid to flood and fire affected communities after major disaster events.
•	The City of Cape Town makes Grants-in-Aid available to organisations to fund projects that benefit the community and assist the City in realising its goals and objectives as set out by the Integrated Development Plan. Through this programme, funding is made available to organisations involved in feeding schemes and the provision of food for the poor (food gardens and soup kitchens)
The Western Cape Department of Health Annual Report 2023/2024 included to budgetary items relating to food procurement. The department has been responsible for the Integrated Nutrition Plan (INP), which is an umbrella for various direct and indirect nutrition interventions. Linked to the INP, the City's Health Department is implementing the Nutrition Therapeutic Programme (NTP). The NTP is a short-term direct intervention providing specialized nutrition products to address malnutrition in undernourished or nutritionally compromised patients. 

Finally, the City's Climate Change Hazard, Vulnerability, and Risk Assessment study has projected drastic temperature increases that will pose a risk to food security as it contributes to enhance evaporation of soil-moisture and surface water resources. This will have detrimental effects in agricultural areas, which lie predominantly outside city boundaries, reinforcing the need to facilitate viable and sustainable urban agriculture within the City and to take action to develop sustainable food systems. In addition, the Provincial Government previously conducted two studies 1) Comparing the Carbon Footprint of Urban Vs Rural Agriculture and 2) Carbon Footprint of “Average” Food Baskets in South Africa.

No Município de Braga, a aquisição de alimentos para as instalações de propriedade e/ou operadas pelo governo, particularmente nas escolas, é uma tarefa crucial para garantir a alimentação saudável e nutritiva da população. A decomposição por grupo de alimentos é fundamental para entender as necessidades nutricionais da comunidade e promover práticas sustentáveis. A preocupação do Município com a utilização de fontes descarbonizadas em suas aquisições reflete um compromisso com a redução da pegada de carbono e a promoção da sustentabilidade.

Os cereais e grãos constituem a base da alimentação e são responsáveis por 40% do total adquirido. Em Braga, a aquisição desse grupo inclui produtos como arroz, massas, pães e leguminosas, como feijão e lentilhas. O município prioriza a compra de alimentos cultivados localmente, muitas vezes utilizando práticas agrícolas que respeitam o meio ambiente e adotam fontes de energia renováveis. Além de oferecer opções integrais nas refeições escolares, essa abordagem não apenas promove uma alimentação mais saudável, mas também apoia a economia local, contribuindo para a redução das emissões de carbono associadas ao transporte de alimentos.

As frutas e vegetais, que representam 30% do total de alimentos adquiridos, são fundamentais para uma dieta equilibrada, pois são ricos em vitaminas, minerais e fibras. No Município de Braga, a oferta inclui uma variedade de produtos sazonais, como maçãs, peras e laranjas, além de vegetais como couve, cenoura e tomate. O município tem estabelecido parcerias com agricultores locais que utilizam práticas agrícolas sustentáveis e técnicas de cultivo que minimizam o uso de recursos não renováveis. Essa iniciativa, juntamente com a educação alimentar nas escolas, incentiva o consumo de frutas e vegetais, contribuindo para a formação de hábitos alimentares saudáveis desde a infância, enquanto se promove a compra de produtos com menor impacto ambiental.

Em relação às carnes e ovos, que representam 20% do total adquirido, são fontes importantes de proteínas essenciais para o crescimento e desenvolvimento. Em Braga, a aquisição deste grupo inclui carnes de frango, bovina e suína, bem como ovos de galinha. O município prioriza a compra de produtos de origem local, garantindo frescura e qualidade. Os programas de nutrição nas escolas enfatizam a moderação no consumo de carnes vermelhas, promovendo alternativas mais saudáveis, como proteínas vegetais.

Os laticínios, que incluem leite, iogurte e queijos, são uma importante fonte de cálcio e proteínas e representam 10% do total de alimentos adquiridos. Em Braga, as aquisições deste grupo são cuidadosamente selecionadas para incluir produtos de qualidade, preferencialmente provenientes de fazendas que utilizam fontes de energia renováveis. O município promove o consumo de laticínios com baixo teor de gordura, contribuindo para uma dieta equilibrada e saudável. A educação alimentar também destaca a importância dos laticínios na prevenção de doenças como a osteoporose, enquanto se esforça para minimizar o impacto ambiental associado à produção desses alimentos.

Hasil - Estimasi Pengadaan Pangan Tahunan (semua fasilitas pemerintah di Manado)
Total (perkiraan): ≈ 52.734 ton pangan / tahun
Rincian menurut kelompok pangan (± ton/tahun):
Serealia (beras & biji-bijian) — ≈ 4.619,5 ton/tahun
Sayur & buah — ≈ 3.464,6 ton/tahun

Lainnya (minyak, bumbu, susu, umbi, camilan) — ≈ 1.154,9 ton/tahun
(Proporsi komposisi: serealia 40% / sayur 30% / protein 20% / lainnya 10%).

Metode Perhitungan
Dasar populasi: menggunakan data penduduk Kota Manado ≈ 483.481 jiwa (RPJMD 2025-2029). 

Identifikasi penerima makan institusi publik:
Sekolah: estimasi jumlah murid sekolah negeri yang mendapat makan.
Rumah sakit: perkiraan jumlah tempat tidur (1,3 per 1.000 penduduk) × tingkat hunian × 3 kali makan/hari.
Panti, penjara, pusat remaja: asumsi 0,5% dari jumlah penduduk × 3 kali makan/hari.
Kantin & fasilitas publik pemerintah: diasumsikan ±5.000 porsi makan/hari.
Konversi ke massa pangan: asumsi rata-rata 0,6 kg per porsi.
Tahunan: porsi per hari × 0,6 kg × 365 hari = total kg → konversi ke ton.
Pembagian kelompok pangan: pakai komposisi rata-rata menu (40% serealia, 30% sayur, 20% protein, 10% lainnya).

Angka Asumsi Utama
Populasi: 483.481 jiwa. 
Sekolah: murid ≈ 30% penduduk → ±144.000 jiwa; tingkat kehadiran 90% → ±129.000; diasumsikan 30% dapat makan sekolah → ±39.162 porsi/hari.
Rumah sakit: ±629 tempat tidur → 70% terisi → ±440 pasien → ±1.320 porsi/hari.
Panti/penjara/rehab: ±2.417 orang → ±7.252 porsi/hari.
Kantin pemerintah: ±5.000 porsi/hari.
Total porsi/hari: ±87.953 → ×0,6 kg → ±52.734 ton/tahun.

Dokumen resmi (RPJMD & Kajian Bappeda) tidak memuat data tonase pangan yang benar-benar dibeli oleh fasilitas pemerintah. Angka di atas murni estimasi berbasis asumsi populasi, kebutuhan makan institusi, dan rata-rata berat makanan.

col4_Comment:
There is no publicly available official report detailing the total quantity of food, measured in tonnes, procured for government-owned and operated facilities in Ca Mau Province. These facilities include municipal buildings, schools, hospitals, youth centers, shelters, public canteens, and prisons.
Despite the absence of a consolidated official figure, an estimation has been conducted based on available public data, including student populations, hospital bed capacities, inmate food allowances, and social protection beneficiary numbers. This estimation, however, is subject to significant limitations due to the lack of precise data on the number of individuals receiving meals in each type of facility and the specific food procurement contracts.
Estimated Food Procurement: A Calculated Approximation
Based on the available data and a set of carefully considered assumptions, it is roughly estimated that government-owned and/or operated facilities in Ca Mau Province procure approximately 1,200 to 1,800 metric tonnes of food annually.
This estimate is broken down as follows:
•	Public Schools: With a student population of approximately 233,222 in the 2023-2024 school year, and assuming that a fraction of these students participate in school meal programs, the estimated food procurement for schools is significant. The calculation is based on the assumption that a certain percentage of students from kindergarten to high school receive at least one meal per day at school, with an average meal size of 250-300 grams. The wide range in the overall estimate is largely due to the uncertainty surrounding the actual coverage of school meal programs. While a 'Healthy School Canteen' model is being implemented, the exact number of participating students remains unclear.
•	Public Hospitals: Ca Mau Province has a number of public hospitals, with the new Ca Mau General Hospital planned to have a capacity of 1,200 beds. Based on older data and the new hospital's capacity, and assuming an average bed occupancy rate and that a majority of inpatients receive three meals a day, a rough estimate of food procurement for the healthcare sector has been calculated.
•	Prisons: Information on the standard monthly food rations for prisoners in Vietnam provides a more solid basis for estimation in this sector. According to national regulations, each inmate is entitled to a specific quantity of rice, meat, fish, vegetables, and other essential food items per month. Based on the number of correctional facilities in the province, a conservative estimate of the inmate population allows for a calculation of the total food provided.
•	Social Protection Centers: These centers in Ca Mau care for several vulnerable individuals, including the elderly, orphans, and people with disabilities. Based on the reported number of residents in these facilities, an estimate of their annual food consumption has been included in the overall calculation.
